text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cabinet to discuss on Saturday draft investment law, which with its assurances and incentives, will pave the way for setting up of 50 industrial areas worth 50 billion pounds.
- Talks between Egypt and Abu Dhabi on joint cooperation, Arab issues and the Middle East peace process.
- Large entry on President Hosni Mubarak in Oxford history encyclopedia.
- France's Le Monde praises Egypt's economy.
- Djibouti president meets Foreign Minister Moussa and invites Mubarak to visit his country.
- Public Enterprise minister says 10 percent of 10 public sector companies will be sold to small investors.
- Foreign Ministry calls in Sudanese ambassador.

- The United States expected to withdraw from Middle East peace process. Washington says Palestinians and Israelis refuse to offer concessions. Albright invites Levy to U.S. to discuss Israel's refusal of the U.S. initiative. Peres says Israeli policy has caused Israel's isolation and division.
- Oil minister says five international companies have began oil exploration in Upper Egypt for the first time in country's history.
- Health minister says there have been 531 Aids cases in Egypt since the 1980s.
- Mubarak to give important political speech today to mark Labour Day.
